Ash broth boiling, foul air bubbling, waves clashing, sound terrifying.
From bottom to top, iron thorns纵横.
On the river banks, sword forests.
Branches, leaves, flowers, fruits all are swords.
Sinners enter the river, following waves up and down.
Tumbling and sinking, iron thorns piercing the body.
Inside and out penetrated, pus and blood flowing out.
Suffering myriad pains, thus they do not die.
Then leave the ash river, reach the opposite shore.
Sharp swords cutting and piercing the body, wounds breaking open.
Again jackals and wolves come to bite the sinners, eating their flesh alive.
Climbing up the sword tree, sword blades pointing downward.
Descending the sword tree, sword blades pointing upward.
Hands grasping, hands severed; feet stepping, feet cut off.
Skin and flesh falling off, only white bones remaining, sinews and veins connected.
Then on the sword tree are iron-beaked crows.
Pecking heads, eating brains, suffering and wailing, thus they do not die.
Return into the ash river, following waves sinking.
Iron thorns piercing the body, suffering myriad pains.
Skin and flesh rotting, pus and blood flowing out.
Only white bones floating outside.
Cold wind blows, quickly they stand up.
Dragged by past karma, unknowingly suddenly arrive at the Iron Balls hell.
There are hot iron balls, hell demons drive and throw them.
Hands and feet rotten, whole body ablaze.
Ten thousand torments arriving, thus they do not die.
After long suffering, then leave the Iron Balls, arrive at the Axes hell.
Seize these sinners, throw them on hot iron.
With hot iron axes, chopping their hands, feet, ears, nose, and body.
Suffering and wailing, yet still not dying.
After long suffering, leave the Axes hell, arrive at the Jackals and Wolves hell.
There are packs of jackals and wolves competing to bite and gnaw.
Flesh falling, bones injured, pus and blood flowing out.
Suffering myriad pains, thus they do not die.
After long suffering, then leave the Jackals and Wolves, arrive at the Sword Tree hell.
Entering that sword forest, a violent wind arises.
Blowing sword tree leaves falling on their bodies.
Heads, faces, bodies all injured and ruined.
Iron-beaked crows peck their two eyes.
Suffering and wailing, thus they do not die.
After long suffering, then leave the Sword Tree, arrive at the Cold Ice hell.
There is a great cold wind blowing on their bodies.
Whole body frozen, skin and flesh falling off.
Suffering and crying, then life ends.
Body doing unwholesome deeds, speech and mind likewise.
Thus falling into the Saṃjīva hell, terrified, hair standing on end.
The Great Hell of Black Ropes.
There are sixteen smaller hells surrounding it on all sides.
Each measures five hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
Why is it called Black Ropes?
The hell wardens seize the sinners and throw them onto hot iron plates.
They stretch out their bodies and straighten them with hot iron ropes.
With hot iron axes, they chop along the rope lines, cutting the sinners into hundreds and thousands of pieces.
Furthermore, they bind them with iron ropes and saw them apart.
Furthermore, countless hot iron ropes are suspended, crisscrossing.
The sinners are driven and forced to walk among the ropes.
Violent winds arise, blowing the iron ropes to entangle and wrap around their bodies.
Their skin is burned through, their flesh scorched, their bones charred, and their marrow boiled, with ten thousand kinds of bitter poisons.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die.
Hence it is called Black Ropes.
After suffering for a long time, they then leave the Black Ropes Hell and arrive at the Black Sand Hell.
And so on until the Icy Cold Hell, after which their lives end.
Having malicious intent towards parents, the Buddha, and his disciples,
one falls into the Black Ropes Hell, where the pain and suffering are beyond description.
The Great Hell of Crushing.
There are sixteen smaller hells surrounding it.
Each measures five hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
Why is it called Crushing?
There are two great stone mountains facing each other.
When people enter between them,
the mountains naturally close together, crushing their bodies.
Their bones and flesh are ground to pulp, and then the mountains return to their original positions.
With ten thousand kinds of bitter poisons, they are not allowed to die.
Furthermore, there are great iron elephants, their entire bodies ablaze, roaring as they charge forward.
They trample the sinners, who writhe upon them.
Their bodies are crushed to pulp, and pus and blood flow out.
Wailing and crying bitterly, they are not allowed to die.
Furthermore, the sinners are seized and laid upon large stones, crushed with great rocks.
Furthermore, the sinners are taken and laid on the ground, pounded with iron pestles.
From their feet to their heads, their skin and flesh are ground to pulp.
Pus and blood flow out, and ten thousand poisons arrive together.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die; hence it is called Crushing.
After suffering for a long time, they then leave the Crushing Hell and arrive at the Black Sand Hell.
And so on until the Icy Cold Hell, after which their lives end.
Merely committing the three evil deeds and not cultivating the three good practices,
one falls into the Crushing Hell, where the pain and suffering are beyond description.
The Great Hell of Wailing.
There are sixteen smaller hells.
Each measures five hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
Why is it called the Wailing Hell?
The hell wardens seize the sinners and throw them into large cauldrons.
They are also placed in large iron pots.
Boiling hot water surges and bubbles, cooking the sinners.
They wail and cry out, in bitter pain and anguish.
Furthermore, they take those sinners and throw them onto iron griddles.
Turned over and roasted, they wail and cry out.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die; hence it is called Wailing.
After suffering for a long time, they then leave the Wailing Hell and arrive at the Black Sand Hell.
And so on until the Icy Water Hell, after which their lives end.
Harboring hatred and poison, committing all evil deeds,
one falls into the Wailing Hell.
The Great Hell of Great Wailing.
There are sixteen smaller hells.
Why is it called Great Wailing?
They take those sinners and place them in large iron pots.
They are also placed in iron cauldrons.
Boiling hot water surges and bubbles, cooking the sinners.
They are also thrown onto large griddles.
Turned over and roasted, they wail and cry out loudly, in bitter pain and anguish.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die; hence it is called Great Wailing.
After suffering for a long time, they leave the Great Wailing Hell and arrive at the Icy Cold Hell.
Then their lives end.
Practicing various wrong views,
being dragged by the net of desire,
committing base and vile deeds,
one falls into the Great Wailing Hell.
The Hell of Burning.
There are sixteen smaller hells.
Why is it called Burning?
They take the sinners and place them in an iron city.
The city is ablaze, red-hot inside and out, burning the sinners.
They are also placed on iron towers.
The towers are ablaze, red-hot inside and out.
They are also thrown into large iron urns.
The urns are ablaze, red-hot inside and out.
The sinners are burned, their skin and flesh charred and rotten, with ten thousand poisons arriving together.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die.
Hence it is called Burning.
After suffering for a long time, they leave the Burning Hell and arrive at the Black Sand Hell.
And so on until the Icy Cold Hell, after which their lives end.
Engaging in burning deeds, one falls into the Burning Hell.
For long nights, they suffer the pain of burning.
The Great Hell of Great Burning.
There are sixteen smaller hells.
Each measures five hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
They take the sinners and place them in an iron city.
The city is ablaze, red-hot inside and out.
The sinners are burned, their skin and flesh charred and rotten, with ten thousand poisons arriving together.
There is a great fire pit with fiercely blazing flames.
On both sides of the pit are great fire mountains.
They seize those sinners, impale them on iron forks, and stand them in the fire, burning them repeatedly until their skin and flesh are charred and rotten.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die.
After suffering for a long time, they leave the Great Burning Hell and arrive at the Black Sand Hell.
And so on until the Icy Cold Hell, after which their lives end.
Abandoning good karmic fruits and engaging in all evil deeds,
one falls into the Great Burning Hell.
The Great Hell of the Uninterrupted.
There are sixteen smaller hells.
Each measures five hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
They seize those sinners and peel off their skin from their feet to the crown of their heads.
Then they wrap the sinners' bodies with their own skin.
They are placed on fire-wheeled carts and run over the hot iron ground.
Circling back and forth, their bodies are crushed and mangled.
Their skin and flesh fall off, and ten thousand poisons arrive together, yet they are not allowed to die.
Furthermore, there is an iron city with fire rising on all four sides.
The flames from the east reach the west, and the flames from the west reach the east.
North, south, up, and down are also like this.
The flames blaze and swirl, leaving no empty space.
Running east and west, their bodies are burned, their skin and flesh charred and rotten.
In bitter pain and anguish, ten thousand poisons arrive together.
The sinners are inside for a long time until a gate opens.
All those sinners run and rush towards it.
Flames shoot out from all their limbs and joints.
Just as they are about to reach the gate, it naturally closes.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are not allowed to die.
Furthermore, the sinners there, whatever they see with their eyes, only see evil sights.
Their ears hear evil sounds, their noses smell foul odors.
Their bodies feel painful touches, and their minds think of evil dharmas.
In the snap of a finger, there is not a moment without suffering.
Hence it is called the Uninterrupted Hell.
After suffering for a long time, their lives end.
Due to heavy sinful deeds, they are reborn in evil destinies.
And so on until the Icy Cold Hell.
Then their lives end.
Due to heavy sinful deeds and the karma of being reborn in evil destinies,
they fall into the Uninterrupted Hell, where the sins are beyond description.
Each of the eight great hells has sixteen smaller hells.
Between the two great diamond mountains,
a great wind arises, named Sāṃkhya.
If this wind were to reach the Four Continents and the eighty-thousand worlds,
all the great mountains on earth, ten li above the ground,
or even a hundred li, would be blown into the air and completely pulverized.
Like a strong man scattering light chaff into the air with his hand.
Because the two great mountains block this wind,
if this wind were to reach the Four Continents,
all the streams, rivers, lakes, and seas among the beings there would dry up and wither.
Moreover, the wind between the mountains is foul, impure, putrid, and extremely pungent.
If it were to reach the Four Continents,
it would fumigate all beings, causing them to lose their eyesight.
Furthermore, these two mountains bring many benefits.
This is also the result of the karmic retribution of beings' actions.
Between the two mountains, there are ten hells.
The first is called Hòuyún.
The second is called Wúyún.
The third is called Hēhē.
The fourth is called Nàihé.
The fifth is called Yángmíng.
The sixth is called Xūgāntí.
The seventh is called Yōubōluó.
The eighth is called Jūwùtóu.
The ninth is called Fēntuólì.
The tenth is called Bōtóumó.
Why is it called Hòuyún?
The sinners in this hell naturally grow bodies,
like thick clouds, hence the name Hòuyún.
Why is it called Wúyún?
The beings grow bodies like chunks of meat, hence the name Wúyún.
Why is it called Hēhē?
When the pain reaches their bodies, they all cry out "hēhē," hence the name Hēhē.
Why is it called Nàihé?
The suffering beings, in their bitter and sour pain with nowhere to turn, all cry out "nàihé," hence the name Nàihé.
Why is it called Yángmíng?
The suffering beings, in their bodily pain, wish to raise their voices and speak, but their tongues cannot turn, so they bleat like sheep, hence the name Yángmíng.
Why is it called the Xūgāntí flower?
The hell is all black like the color of the Xūgāntí flower.
Why is it called the Yōubōluó flower?
The hell is all blue like the Yōubōluó flower.
Why is it called the Jūwùtóu flower?
The hell is all red like the color of the Jūwùtóu flower.
Why is it called the Fēntuólì flower?
The hell is all white like the Fēntuólì flower.
Why is it called the Bōtóumó flower?
The hell is all crimson like the color of the Bōtóumó flower.
For example, suppose there is a basket holding sixty-four hú full of sesame seeds.
Every hundred years, someone takes one sesame seed away.
Continuing like this until it is emptied,
the suffering in the Hòuyún hell would still not be finished.
The lifespan of twenty Hòuyún hells
equals the lifespan of one Wúyún hell.
The lifespan of twenty Wúyún hells
equals the lifespan of one Hēhē hell.
The lifespan of twenty Hēhē hells
equals the lifespan of one Nàihé hell.
The lifespan of twenty Nàihé hells
equals the lifespan of one Yángmíng hell.
The lifespan of twenty Yángmíng hells
equals the lifespan of one Xūgāntí hell.
The lifespan of twenty Xūgāntí hells
equals the lifespan of one Yōubōluó hell.
The lifespan of twenty Yōubōluó hells
equals the lifespan of one Jūwùtóu hell.
The lifespan of twenty Jūwùtóu hells
equals the lifespan of one Fēntuólì hell.
The lifespan of twenty Fēntuólì hells
equals the lifespan of one Bōtóumó hell.
The lifespan of twenty Bōtóumó hells is called one intermediate kalpa.
Twenty intermediate kalpas are called one great kalpa.
In the Bōtóumó hell, the flames are extremely fierce.
When sinners are one hundred yojanas away from the fire,
they are already scorched; at sixty yojanas,
their ears are already deaf, hearing nothing.
At fifty yojanas, their eyes are already blind, seeing nothing.
The monk Qūbōlì, harboring evil intentions,
slandered Shèlìfú and Mùjiānlián.
After his body perished and his life ended, he fell into this Bōtóumó hell.
The Avīci hell is eight thousand yojanas in length, width, and height.
It has seven layers of iron walls and seven layers of iron nets.
Below are eighteen compartments.
Surrounding it are seven layers,
all of which are forests of knives.
There are also seven layers of sword forests.
At the four corners are four large bronze dogs,
forty yojanas in length and width.
Their eyes are like lightning,
their fangs like sword trees,
their teeth like knife mountains,
their tongues like iron thorns.
All the hair on their bodies burns with fierce fire.
Their smoke is foul and vile.
There are eighteen jailers,
with mouths like yakṣas.
Their sixty-four eyes shoot out iron pellets.
The dogs' fangs protrude upward, four yojanas high.
Fire flows from the tips of the fangs, burning and frying iron chariots.
Wheel nets emit fire.
Blades, swords, and halberds burn the Avīci city until it is red like molten bronze.
The jailers have eight heads and sixty horns.
Fire burns at the tips of the horns.
The fire transforms into bronze, which then becomes knife wheels.
They follow one another amidst the flames,
filling the Avīci city.
Inside the city are seven iron pillars.
Fire surges like boiling iron, flowing and gushing out of the four gates.
Above are eighteen cauldrons.
Boiling bronze surges and overflows, filling the city.
Between every two compartments are eighty-four thousand large iron pythons and serpents.
They spew poisonous fire, their bodies filling the city.
These serpents roar like heavenly thunder.
They rain down five hundred large iron pellets.
Also, five hundred million insects,
with eighty-four thousand mouths, spew fire like rain falling down,
filling the Avīci city.
When these insects descend, the fierce fire blazes, illuminating eighty-four thousand yojanas above the hell.
It rushes into the great sea, under the Wòjiāo mountain, piercing the sea bottom, dripping like cart axles.
If someone kills their father, harms their mother, insults and shames their six kinds of relatives,
at the time of death, bronze dogs transform into eighteen chariots,
shaped like jeweled canopies.
All the flames transform into jade maidens.
The sinners see them from afar, their hearts delighted, and wish to go.
When the wind knives dismember them, they shiver from cold and lose their voices.
They would rather have good fire placed on the chariots to burn themselves.
Immediately, their lives end.
They sit on golden chariots, gazing at the jade maidens,
who all grasp iron axes to chop and slice their bodies.
In the time it takes to bend or stretch an arm, they fall straight into Avīci.
From the upper compartments, like spinning fire wheels, they descend to the lower compartments.
Their bodies fill the compartments.
The bronze dogs roar loudly, gnawing their bones and sucking their marrow.
The jailers and rākṣasas seize large axes to chop them, then pierce their necks with tridents, making them rise, their bodies covered in flames filling the Avīci hell.
King Yánluó loudly proclaims:
"Foolish hell-dweller,
when you were in the world,
you were unfilial to your parents, wicked, arrogant, and without virtue.
Now your place of birth is called the Avīci hell."
The jailers then
move from the lower compartments back up to the upper compartments,
passing through eighty-four thousand compartments, hanging the bodies as they go, reaching the iron net boundary.
One day and night here equals sixty small kalpas in Jambudvīpa.
After one great kalpa ends,
those who commit the five heinous crimes,
at the time of death,
are dismembered by eighteen wind knives like iron fire chariots.
Due to the intense heat, they think:
"Wouldn't it be joyful to have beautiful flowers and cool, large trees to play under?"
When this thought arises, the eighty-four thousand evil sword forests
transform into jeweled trees with lush flowers and fruits, arrayed before them.
The great fiery flames transform into lotus flowers.
The sinners, faster than a rainstorm, sit on the lotus flowers.
Iron-mouthed insects rise from the fiery flowers, piercing their bones and entering their bodies, causing agitation.
All the sword branches
slice their flesh and bones.
Innumerable knife forests descend from above.
Fire chariots, furnace coals, and eighteen kinds of suffering appear all at once to greet them.
When this vision appears, they sink into the ground.
From the lower compartments, their bodies rise like blooming flowers, filling the lower compartments, while fire blazes below.
Reaching the upper compartments, their bodies fill them.
Due to the intense heat and distress, they open their eyes and stick out their tongues.
Trillions of molten bronze drops and hundreds of thousands of knife wheels
descend from the sky, entering through their necks and exiting through their feet.
All the sufferings exceed those described above by hundreds of thousands of times.
Those who commit the five heinous crimes suffer for five kalpas.
There are also beings
who violate the four grave prohibitions, consume offerings deceitfully, slander with wrong views, and do not understand cause and effect.
They abandon the study of prajñā, slander the buddhas of the ten directions,
steal from the saṅgha, engage in unrestrained lust,
and force themselves upon pure nuns, sisters, and female relatives.
Those who commit such evil deeds
will, at the time of death,
have their bodies dismembered by wind knives, lying restlessly as if beaten with rods.
Their minds become confused, and they develop mad, deluded thoughts.
They see their own houses, men, women, young and old,
all as impure things.
Filth, urine, and foul places overflow outside.
The jailers and rākṣasas lift them with large iron tridents.
The Avīci hell and all the knife forests
transform into jeweled trees and cool ponds.
The flames transform into golden-leafed lotus flowers, and the iron-mouthed insects transform into ducks and geese.
The sounds of suffering are like singing.
The sinners hear this and think, "I shall roam there."
They sit on fiery lotus flowers.
Various creatures compete to devour them.
Dogs eat their hearts.
In an instant,
their bodies become like iron flowers filling the eighteen compartments.
Such sinners undergo eighty-four thousand great kalpas,
then enter the eighteen compartments in the east,
suffering as before.
The south, west, and north are also like this.
Those who slander the Vaipulya sūtras,
commit the five heinous crimes,
destroy the saṅgha,
defile bhikṣuṇīs,
sever all good roots,
and possess numerous crimes fill the Avīci hell with their bodies.
Their four limbs also fill the eighteen compartments.
This Avīci hell burns only such hell-dwelling beings.
When the kalpa is about to end, the eastern gate opens.
Outside the eastern gate,
clear springs, flowing water, flower and fruit trees all appear.
The sinners see light from the lower compartments as the fire temporarily subsides.
They rise from the lower compartments,
crawling on their bellies, twisting and turning.
They climb upward to the upper compartments.
At that time, hot iron pellets rain from the sky.
They run to the eastern gate, and upon reaching the threshold,
the jailers and rākṣasas seize iron tridents and pierce their eyes.
Iron dogs gnaw their hearts, and they faint and die.
The south, west, and north gates are also like this.
They undergo half a kalpa.
The Avīci Hell.
There are eighteen lesser hells.
The lesser hells.
Each has eighteen cold hells.
Eighteen dark hells.
Eighteen lesser hot hells.
Eighteen blade-wheel hells.
Eighteen sword-wheel hells.
Eighteen fire-cart hells.
Eighteen boiling-excrement hells.
Eighteen cauldron-soup hells.
Eighteen ash-river hells.
Five hundred million sword-forest hells.
Five hundred million thorn-forest hells.
Five hundred million bronze-pillar hells.
Five hundred million iron-millstone hells.
Five hundred million iron-rim hells.
Eighteen iron-cavern hells.
Eighteen iron-pellet hells.
Eighteen sharp-stone hells.
Eighteen drink-copper hells.
Such are the many hells.
The Avīci Hell.
Dying and being reborn amidst freezing ice.
Dying in the freezing-ice hell and being reborn in a place of darkness.
For eighty million years, the eyes see nothing.
Receiving the body of a great insect, writhing and crawling on its belly.
All faculties are blocked and obscured, being eaten by foxes and wolves.
Afterwards born as an animal.
For fifty million lifetimes receiving the forms of birds and beasts.
Then reborn among humans.
With the six sense faculties incomplete, impoverished and lowly.
After five hundred lifetimes, born as a hungry ghost.
Afterwards encountering a good spiritual friend and arousing the mind of Bodhi.
The eighteen cold hells are thus:
Eight-directional ice mountains.
The mountains have eighteen partitions.
Furthermore, there are eighteen lesser ice mountains.
Between the freezing ice mountains, like tile lotuses.
Eighteen yojanas high.
Above are ice wheels.
Their length and breadth are exactly twelve yojanas.
Like heavenly hail falling from the sky.
Robbing, plundering, stealing, stripping, freezing, and killing beings.
When this person's karmic retribution nears its end and life is about to cease,
all blade-winds transform into scorching fire.
The sinner thinks, "Why do I not now lie upon the ice?"
Having this thought,
the hell wardens, the rākṣasas, holding ice wheels, arrive treading the void.
The sinner, seeing them, feels affection and longing in his heart.
His breath ceases, life ends, and he is reborn on an ice mountain.
After being reborn,
the eighteen ice mountains are as if fanned by a fan.
All the freezing ice enters through his pores.
Among the eighteen partitions, one partition becomes completely filled.
Splitting, cracking, and breaking apart like red lotus flowers.
Ice wheels above and below completely cover his body.
The eight-directional ice mountains simultaneously close together.
No other words remain, only "Ara."
At that time, the sinner thereupon has this thought:
"When will I ever escape this freezing ice and be born amidst scorching fire?"
At that time, in the sky are iron-beaked birds.
Spitting fire, breaking the ice, pecking at brains.
The sinner immediately dies.
The hell wardens again strike the ground with iron tridents, shouting "Huóhuó!" (Alive! Alive!).
Responding to the sound, he immediately revives.
His body fiercely ablaze, he wishes for the previous ice to extinguish this fire.
The hell wardens again receive him with ice wheels and place him in the hell.
Thus, among the eighteen partitions, none are not experienced.
The lifespan in years in this cold hell,
is like the eight million years of the sun and moon in the Heaven of the Four Heavenly Kings.
The retribution ended, he is born lowly, impoverished, and base.
For fifty lifetimes, a slave or servant among humans.
Clothes not covering the body, food not filling the mouth.
This retribution finished,
he encounters a good spiritual friend and arouses the mind of Bodhi.
The dark hells are thus:
Eighteen layers of black mountains.
Eighteen layers of black nets.
Eighteen layers of iron beds.
Eighteen layers of iron veils.
One mountain is eighty-four thousand yojanas high.
Each veil is also eighty-four thousand yojanas thick.
Between each veil are eighteen layers of iron mountains, rākṣasas like a forest.
These mountains are dark and shadowy.
Stealing the lamps and lights of the Buddha and the Saṅgha.
Stealing from parents and teachers.
Slandering Dharma preachers.
Also destroying worldly debate masters and such.
Disregarding respect and seniority, knowing no shame or remorse.
Due to these sins, when life is about to end,
the eyes have lightning flashes, flickering incessantly.
He then thinks:
"What sin have I committed to always see this fire?"
He closes both eyes, not wishing to see.
When life is about to end,
the hell wardens, the rākṣasas, lift great iron beds, spread out great iron wheels.
Like a great troop of cloud-riders.
Arriving through the sky.
Formless yet having sound.
The sinner, about to go, life ending,
sits on an iron bed, falling into a dark place.
Blade wheels above and below chop and sever his body.
There are great iron crows with long, sharp beaks and claws.
Flying down from the mountains to seize the sinner.
In extreme pain, he runs swiftly, seeking light but finding none.
Underfoot, caltrops pierce bones and penetrate marrow.
Thus in panic and terror, for five hundred trillion years, the sun and moon as before.
That person's head strikes the various dark mountains.
Brains flow, eyes pop out.
The hell wardens, the rākṣasas, with iron tridents, place them in the eye sockets.
The retribution finished, he then emerges.
As a poor person.
Eyes squinting, blind and sightless.
Or driven away by leprous patients.
Such karmic retribution for five hundred lifetimes.
After that, he encounters a good spiritual friend and arouses the mind of Bodhi.
The eighteen lesser hot hells are thus:
Like the Avīci Hell.
Also seven-layered cities, seven-layered iron rims.
Immeasurable evils serve as adornments.
Due to not following the teacher's instruction, giving rise to a wicked, rebellious mind.
Not knowing gratitude, stealing from the teacher, harming the teacher.
Defiling the teacher's pure food, sitting on the teacher's seat, taking the teacher's alms bowl, hiding it, making it impure.
Making various evil poisons for the teacher to drink.
Whether śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa.
Committing various unlawful acts without shame or remorse.
Stripping images, breaking stūpas, robbing Dharma treasures and objects.
Killing uncles, aunts, parents, brothers, sisters.
When life is about to end,
eighteen hell wardens each use iron tridents to lift and place him in one partitioned hell.
Like a great jeweled canopy raining fine drizzle.
Raindrops like flowers, heat and torment enter the heart.
Seeing the rain as cool, he then thinks:
"May I get to sit under the shade of the canopy.
Cool rain sprinkling me, would that not be pleasant?"
Breath ceases, life ends.
In a mere instant, he sits upon a sword forest.
A hundred million sword blades.
Each blade emits fire, burning and piercing his body.
The jeweled canopy in the sky transforms into a fire wheel.
Descending from above, directly splitting his crown.
The body shatters into several thousand pieces.
From above rain copper pellets, entering through the pores.
Hell wardens, rākṣasas, with great iron tridents, stab the sinner's eyes.
Or with iron arrows, pierce and shoot his heart; he faints and dies.
In a moment, he revives, sitting on a sword bed.
A violent whirlwind blows him down into hell.
Then King Yama declares:
"Hell-being, you committed many evils.
Killing your teacher, slandering your teacher.
Your place of birth now is called the Tongue-Extracting Avīci.
You shall be in this hell for three kalpas."
Having said this, he disappears and is no longer seen.
The blade-wheel hells are thus:
Four-sided blade mountains.
Among the many mountains, blades accumulate like wheels.
There are eight hundred million extremely large blade wheels.
Following in succession descending like raindrops.
Taking pleasure in tormenting others, killing beings.
At the time of death,
suffering from rebellious qi illness, the heart hard as stone.
He then makes this wish:
"If I could get a sharp blade to cut away these afflictions, would that not be a relief?"
At that time, the hell wardens, wearing blade wheels on their heads, obscure them so they are not seen.
Coming before the sinner, with humble words and deferential speech,
"I have a sharp blade able to cut away grave illness."
The sinner rejoices and thinks to himself:
"Only this would bring relief."
Breath ceases, life ends, born upon a blade wheel.
Like a drunken elephant running, falling amidst blade mountains.
At that time, the four mountains simultaneously close together.
Four kinds of blade mountains cut and slice his body.
Unable to bear it, he faints and dies.
Hell wardens, rākṣasas, drive and press the sinner.
Making him climb the blade mountain, coming to the mountain peak.
Blades wound from the feet up to the heart.
Fearing the hell wardens, he crawls upward on hands and knees.
Having reached the mountain peak,
the hell wardens, hands holding all manner of tree branches.
Before death, iron dogs gnaw his heart, a hundred kinds of excruciating pain.
Iron worms nibble and eat until the flesh is completely gone.
Immediately they again shout "Alive!"
Feet wearing iron wheels, descending from the sky.
In one day and one night, six billion births and six billion deaths.
Such numerous times, like the lifespan of the Four Heavenly Kings, eighty million years.
The retribution finished, he then emerges, falling among animals.
For five hundred lifetimes, having to feed many mouths.
Again for five hundred lifetimes receiving a lowly, base form.
Afterwards encountering a good spiritual friend and arousing the mind of Bodhi.
The Sword-Wheel Hell:
It measures fifty yojanas in length, breadth, and height.
It is filled with sword-trees, their number
like rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.
Each sword-tree is forty yojanas high.
Eighty-four thousand sword-wheels serve as its leaves,
eighty-four thousand sword-wheels as its flowers,
eighty-four thousand sword-wheels as its fruit,
and eighty-four thousand boiling copper [wheels] as its branches.
Due to taking pleasure in killing without satiety,
such sinners, when approaching the end of life,
encounter a great feverish illness and then think:
"My body now is sometimes hot, sometimes cold.
My entire body is stiff and hard like an iron anvil."
They then make a wish:
"If I could obtain a vajra sword to cut away this affliction, the joy would be beyond words."
At that time, the hell-wardens transform themselves
into the forms of the sinner's own parents, relatives, or friends.
Appearing before the person, they tell them:
"I have a secret method, just as you wish; I shall give it to you."
The sinner says: "Quickly, quickly, I desire it!"
Their breath ceases and life ends; like a horse galloping, they are reborn among the sword-flowers.
Innumerable swords and blades slice their bones, shatter their flesh, scattering it into emptiness.
There are also iron crows
that descend from the trees, gouging out eyes and pecking at ears.
There are great rākṣasas
who grasp iron axes, splitting heads and extracting brains.
Iron dogs come to lick; after death, they are revived by a shout.
Driven to climb the tree,
before reaching the treetop, their bodies are crushed to dust.
In one day and night, their bodies are killed as many times as dust particles, beyond reckoning.
Due to the sin of killing people, they suffer such calamities for eighty trillion years, then are born among animals.
Their bodies constantly bear heavy burdens; after death, they are skinned again.
After five hundred lifetimes, they are reborn among humans,
poor, short-lived, sickly, and emaciated.
After this, encountering a good spiritual friend, they arouse the mind of bodhi.
The Fire-Chariot Hell:
Each copper cauldron
measures forty yojanas in length, breadth, and height.
It is filled with fire.
Below are twelve wheels,
above are nine thousand and four fire-wheels.
There are beings who, as disciples of the Buddha,
or serving the ninety-six kinds of Brahmā,
or as householders, deceive and mislead through wrong livelihood, flattery, and wickedness.
Such sinners, when life is about to end,
first have the wind element agitated; their bodies become cold as ice.
They then think:
"When will I obtain a great mass of fierce fire?
If I could sit within it, I would forever be rid of this cold sickness."
Having thought this,
the hell-warden rākṣasas transform into a fire-chariot like a golden lotus flower.
The hell-warden sits atop it, appearing like a youth,
holding a white whisk, dancing and drumming as he arrives.
The sinner becomes attached and enamored,
thinking: "If I sit upon this, the pleasure would be beyond words."
Their breath ceases and life ends; they are loaded onto the fire-chariot.
Their limbs and joints burn with fire, their bodies scorched and scattered.
The hell-warden shouts to revive them, and they immediately come back to life.
The fire-chariot crushes their bodies a full eighteen times, shattering them to dust.
Heaven rains boiling copper, sprinkling it all over their bodies, and they are revived again.
Thus they go back and forth, rising to the edge of the boiling liquid and falling back into the cauldron.
Crushed by the fire-chariot, in one day and night they die nine billion times and are reborn nine billion times.
When this person's sin is exhausted, they are born into a poor and lowly family, serving others,
bound to them, without autonomy.
Only after repaying the offerings [they wrongly received] do they, after a long time, gain liberation.
Due to the meritorious virtue of their earlier renunciation and good heart,
they encounter a good spiritual friend who expounds the Dharma for them.
Their mind opens, understanding dawns, and they become arhats.
The Boiling Excrement Hell:
Eighty yojanas in size, with eighteen iron cities.
Each iron city has eighteen compartments.
In each compartment, the four walls all have billions of sword-trees.
The ground is like knife blades,
the blades three feet thick.
Upon these blades are hundreds of thousands of caltrops, beyond reckoning.
Between each caltrop and sword-tree
grow iron worms, countless in number.
Each iron worm has hundreds of thousands of heads,
each head has hundreds of thousands of mouths,
and each mouth has hundreds of thousands of venomous worms.
These venomous worms spew hot excrement,
boiling like molten copper, filling the iron enclosure.
Above are iron nets and iron crows.
For violating the eight precepts of the uposatha,
defiling śrāmaṇerikās and śikṣamāṇās,
defiling the precepts of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
defiling the precepts of upāsakas and upāsikās,
these seven categories and all others,
defiling the pure food of the saṅgha, defiling the food of parents,
stealing and eating first, handling with impure hands,
and, as a saṅgha official, out of arrogance defiling the pure food of the saṅgha,
disciples of the four assemblies sitting on saṅgha seats with impure bodies,
committing sthūlātyaya offenses and not repenting for a long time,
consuming the saṅgha's food falsely, sitting among the saṅgha assembly during the uposatha,
such numerous, immeasurable sinners of impure evil karma—
when approaching the end of life, their entire bodies become fragrant,
like musk deer, unbearably so.
They then think:
"Where can I go to not smell this fragrance?"
The hell-warden transforms into a form like a painted vase containing filth and excrement,
approaches the sinner and touches them with his hand,
causing that sinner's mind to become attached and enamored.
Their breath ceases and life ends; they fall into the boiling excrement.
Their bodies putrefy and rot; many worms devour them, slicing to the bone and penetrating the marrow.
Driven by thirst, they drink the hot boiling excrement.
Venomous worms and maggots devour their tongue roots.
In one day and night, they are born nine billion times and die nine billion times.
When their sin is exhausted, they are born into a poor and lowly family, without autonomy.
Even if born in the world, they constantly encounter evil kings and belong to masters of wrong views.
All kinds of evil affairs oppress and afflict their bodies.
Tumors, swellings, and malignant sores serve as their clothing.
Due to the good causes and conditions of having heard the Dharma in past lives,
they encounter a good spiritual friend, leave home to study the Path, and become arhats.
The Eighteen Cauldron-Boiling Hell:
There are eighteen cauldrons,
each measuring forty yojanas in length, breadth, and height.
Seven layers of iron nets, filled with boiling iron.
Five hundred rākṣasas stoke great charcoal stones,
burning the copper cauldrons, flames blazing in succession.
For sixty days, the fire cannot be extinguished.
One day in Jambudvīpa equals one hundred twenty thousand years.
The boiling liquid in the cauldrons surges upward, transforming into fire-wheels,
then returns into the cauldrons.
For destroying the Buddha's prohibitions and precepts, killing for sacrificial offerings,
for the sake of eating meat, burning mountains and wilderness, harming beings,
eating beings alive, burning them with fire—
such sinners, when life is about to end,
experience physical and mental distress, losing control of urine and feces.
Sometimes hot as boiling water, sometimes cold as ice,
they then think:
"If I could get into a large warm bath to bathe, wouldn't that be joyful?"
The hell-warden rākṣasas transform into servants,
holding basins of hot water, arriving before the sinner.
The sinner's mind becomes fond and delighted.
Their breath ceases and life ends; they are born in the boiling cauldrons.
Swiftly they dissolve and rot, only bones remaining.
An iron fork fishes them out; iron dogs gnaw on them.
Vomited onto the ground, they quickly revive again.
The hell-wardens drive and urge them, forcing them back into the cauldrons.
Because the iron cauldrons are hot, they climb the sword-trees.
Their bones and flesh break and fall into the boiling cauldrons.
In one day and night, they die and are born as many times as the sands of the Ganges.
When their sin is exhausted, they are born as pigs, sheep, chickens, or dogs.
All places of short lifespan they experience without exception.
Thus they receive such bodies for eighty million years.
After life ends, they are reborn among humans,
receiving two kinds of retribution:
first, much illness;
second, short lifespan.
After passing countless kalpas, they encounter a good spiritual friend,
receive and uphold the five precepts, practice the six pāramitās.
The Ash-River Hell:
It is two hundred yojanas long,
twelve yojanas wide.
Below are sharp knives; on the banks are sword-trees.
It is filled with fierce fire, twelve fathoms wide.
Moreover, there is molten ash covering the fire,
forty fathoms thick.
For stealing from parents, teachers, good friends, brothers, and sisters,
such foolish people have no shame or remorse,
do not recognize kindness and nurture, do not follow their teachers' instructions—
such persons, when the retribution for their sins is about to end life,
have their bellies and hearts filled with qi, breath coming in gasps.
They then think:
"My heart is like mud; qi fills my chest.
If I could get a tiny spark to burn my body, wouldn't that be joyful?"
The hell-warden, responding to their thought, transforms into their wife and children,
holding a fire-brazier with fine ash covering it,
arriving before the sinner.
The sinner rejoices.
Their breath ceases and life ends; they are born in the ash river.
Among the various sword-trees is a rākṣasa
holding a sharp sword, about to come and harm them; terrified, they run into the ash river.
Lifting and lowering their feet, knives wound their feet.
Sword-trees rain knives, entering through their pores.
The rākṣasa uses a fork to fork out their heart.
Collapsing to the ground, they faint and die, then quickly revive again.
In one day and night, they are born five hundred billion times and die five hundred billion times.
Driven by hunger and thirst, they open their mouths to eat.
Sword-trees rain knives, entering through their tongues.
Their bellies split, chests rupture; they faint and die.
Due to having heard the Dharma and the name of the saṅgha in former lives,
after their sin is exhausted, they are born among humans,
poor and lowly.
Perceiving the impermanence of the world, they leave home to study the Path.
If the age is without a Buddha, they become pratyekabuddhas.
If the world has a Buddha, they become arhats.
The Sword Forest Hell.
It is filled with sword trees spanning eight thousand yojanas.
There are red-hot iron pellets that serve as their fruit.
The trees are twenty-four yojanas high.
Because of not filial to parents and not revering teachers and elders,
committing evil speech karma, lacking a compassionate and loving heart, and using blades and staves to harm others,
when nearing death, the mind becomes like sticky paste, clinging to everything.
At that moment, this thought arises:
"My mind is bound and attached, unable to let go of any matter it encounters.
Indulging in wine and lust, even when facing suffering, the mind still does not cease.
If I could obtain a sharp blade to cut off this attachment."
The hell guards respond by transforming into attendants.
Holding a mirror, they say:
"Your mind is full of attachments; you may look into this mirror."
Seeing the image of a sharp sword,
he immediately thinks:
"My body is weak and frail, unable to endure desires.
If I could obtain this sharp sword,
to cut off my mind, would that not be a relief?"
As this thought arises, his breath ceases and life ends, and he receives the body of a hungry ghost.
Among the sword trees, iron pellets transform and appear.
They enter from the top of the head and exit through the intestines, scorching and rotting them.
The hell guards beat and drive him to climb the trees.
Iron-mouthed insects gnaw, terrifying him into climbing the trees.
Thus, he wanders through the entire sword forest.
In one day and one night, he undergoes eighty thousand births and deaths.
After the sin is exhausted, he is born in an age of famine and pestilence.
As a human, he is lowly and despised, his breath constantly foul, and people detest seeing him.
Later, he encounters a virtuous friend and awakens the bodhi mind.
The Thorn Forest Hell.
It is filled with iron thorns spanning eight thousand yojanas.
At the tip of each thorn are twelve swords.
On the trees, there are also large red-hot iron hooks.
Because of evil speech, divisive speech, frivolous speech, and unrighteous speech,
indulging in unrestrained jesting and deceitfully speaking of right and wrong,
criticizing the scriptures and slandering teachers of discourse,
for such retribution of sin, when life is about to end, the throat becomes parched and the tongue dry.
At that moment, this thought arises:
"If I could obtain a sharp thorn to pierce my neck and draw blood,
letting water flow through the vessels, would that not be a relief?"
The hell guards, the rākṣasas, transform into parents, holding bright pearls in their hands.
The pearls have thorns growing from their tips, which they point toward the mouth as if dripping water.
The sinner rejoices, his breath ceases and life ends.
In an instant like lightning, he is born among the thorn forests.
The hell guards, the rākṣasas, hold iron hooks and pull out his tongue.
Eight thousand iron oxen with large iron plows plow through his tongue.
In one day and one night, he undergoes six hundred births and deaths.
After this, he is born among humans.
With narrow shoulders, wrinkled face, and stammering speech,
such a sinner's body grows various sores.
Pus and blood flow abundantly for five hundred lifetimes, and people detest seeing him.
After this, even if he speaks, people do not believe or accept it.
He encounters a virtuous friend and awakens the bodhi mind.
The Copper Pillar Hell.
There is a forest of copper pillars like a fiery mountain.
It is six hundred yojanas high.
Below is a fierce fire, above the fire is an iron bed, and on it are blade wheels.
In between are iron-mouthed insects and iron-beaked crows.
Because of excessive greed and confusion, stained with impure attachments,
engaging in impure acts at improper places and times,
even if there are bhikṣuṇīs, brāhmaṇas, and other practitioners of purity,
if they violate the pure Dharma at improper times and places,
or even all those who commit improper conduct,
such sinners, when nearing death,
their entire bodies become stiff and tremble uncontrollably.
At that moment, this thought arises:
"If I could obtain a firm, large copper or iron pillar,
to bind this body and make it immovable."
The hell guards immediately transform into servants.
Holding iron staffs, they come to the sinner.
They say, "O elder,
your body is now strong, while all else is weak; you may grasp this staff."
His heart rejoices, his breath ceases and life ends.
In the time it takes to grasp the staff, he is born atop the copper pillar.
Fierce flames blaze, burning his body.
Terrified, he looks down and sees on the iron bed
a beautiful woman.
If it is a woman, she sees a handsome man.
With love and attachment arising in the heart, they descend from the copper pillar and fall to the ground.
The copper pillar pierces their bodies, iron nets entangle their necks, and iron-mouthed insects gnaw at their flesh.
They fall onto the iron bed.
Both men and women simultaneously have fire arise from their six sense organs.
Iron-mouthed insects enter from the eyes and exit from the male or female organs.
For those who defile precepts, there are an additional nine hundred million small insects,
like maggots, with twelve mouths.
Fire emerges from their mouths as they gnaw at the body.
In one day and one night, they undergo nine hundred million births and nine hundred million deaths.
Afterward, they are born as pigeons and doves for five hundred lifetimes.
Then they are born among dragons for five hundred lifetimes.
Later, they are born among humans as those without organs, with two organs,
or with indeterminate organs, as eunuchs for five hundred lifetimes.
Even if they become human,
their wives are not chaste, their children are not filial, and their servants do not obey.
After this, they encounter a virtuous friend and awaken the bodhi mind.
The Iron Machine Hell has an iron bed.
It measures four hundred yojanas in length and width.
On it are installed numerous mechanisms.
Between the mechanisms are trillions of iron crossbows.
The iron crossbows have billions of sharp blades on their heads.
Because of greed and desire, they are not filial to parents,
do not revere teachers and elders,
do not follow good teachings, and kill living beings.
When such a person's life ends, the body trembles, and fluids flow from the six orifices.
He sees his own bed as soft as cotton,
thinking, "Would it not be a relief to lie in a firm, cool place?"
The hell guards, the rākṣasas,
carry the bed with a fork, bringing a fiery blanket to the sinner.
Rejoicing, he wishes to lie down.
His breath ceases and life ends, and he is born on the iron machine.
Trillions of iron mechanisms move from below, countless iron mechanisms rise.
The iron crossbows simultaneously draw two iron
arrows that shoot into the sinner's heart.
In one day and one night, he undergoes six hundred billion births and deaths.
Later, he is born among animals for five hundred lifetimes.
Then he is reborn among humans,
poor and lowly, serving others.
Often falling into prisons, constantly receiving whippings.
Later, he encounters a virtuous friend and awakens the bodhi mind.
The Iron Net Hell.
There are eighty-nine layers of iron nets.
Between each net are billions of iron needles.
Each iron needle is equipped with five mechanisms.
Because of deviant minds, flattery, deceit, and seducing others,
harboring slander and malice, with evil thoughts day and night,
when nearing death, the body itches intensely.
At that moment, this thought arises:
"If I could obtain a bundle of needles to prick myself, would that not be a relief?"
As this thought arises, the hell guards transform into good physicians.
Holding sharp needles, they proclaim:
"To cure illness."
The sinner's heart rejoices, his breath ceases and life ends, and he is born among the iron nets.
As his body passes beneath, all mechanisms move.
Countless needles shoot into his pores.
Thus, he twists and turns among the iron nets.
In a mere instant, he undergoes death and rebirth.
After the sin is exhausted, he is born in borderlands without the Buddha-Dharma.
He does not even hear worldly good words, let alone the true Dharma.
Although born among humans, he is encompassed by the three evil paths.
Later, he encounters a virtuous friend; although he hears the Dharma, his mind does not comprehend it.
The Iron Cave Hell.
It is the most severe suffering among the hungry ghost paths.
There is an iron mountain.
It measures twenty-five yojanas in length and width.
On the mountain are five hundred trillion large red-hot iron pellets.
Each iron pellet is perfectly round, measuring thirteen yojanas.
Between the mountains are hundreds of thousands of blades and swords.
At that time, a small opening appears on the eastern side of the mountain.
Like a Magadha measure, black smoke emerges.
Because of miserliness and attachment, the heart is like diamond,
only delighting in seeking and never satisfied.
Not providing for parents, wife, and children,
viewing the teachings of teachers and elders as filth,
not giving clothing or food to servants and relatives,
such a miser does not consider impermanence,
guarding wealth like his own eyes.
When life is about to end, all senses become blocked.
The mouth is locked, unable to speak, but the mind silently thinks:
"After I die, these evil people
will consume my wealth like eating iron pellets,
and inhabit my cave like dwelling in a dark room."
After this thought arises,
the hell guards transform into misers,
gathering much wealth and burning it with fire.
The sinner's heart rejoices, his breath ceases and life ends, and he is born on the fiery mountain.
Like molten copper, he is cast into the iron cave.
Sword insects and blade insects gnaw at his body.
Smoke blinds his eyes, so he cannot see the flames.
Running east and west, his head strikes the iron mountain.
Iron pellets penetrate from the top of his head to his feet.
In a single thought-instant, he undergoes death and rebirth.
After the sin is exhausted, he is born among hungry ghosts.
His body grows to several tens of yojanas.
His throat is like a needle tube, his belly like a great mountain.
Seeking food east and west, molten copper is poured into his throat.
For eight thousand years,
he is born among ghosts that eat pus, saliva, and blood.
Then he is born among latrine spirits, pigs, dogs, and the like.
After the sin is exhausted, he is born in poverty, lowliness, and places without clothing or food.
He encounters a virtuous friend and awakens the bodhi mind.
The Iron Ball Hell.
An iron city eighty yojanas in extent, filled.
Eighty-eight compartments.
In each compartment are five mountains of knives.
They are used to cover the top.
Below are eighteen great evil iron serpents.
All spew iron swords, the tips of the swords blazing with fire.
They slander and insult almsgiving, saying giving brings no reward.
They urge people to hoard and accumulate.
Towards kings, ministers, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and all beings,
they say giving has no cause and also no fruit or reward.
When such a person is nearing death, their neck stiffens and their pulse contracts.
They toss and turn, unable to speak, disliking to see people.
Lying with downcast gaze, in their heart they only think:
"I have accumulated treasures.
If they could go with me, the joy would be indescribable."
The hell guards transform into their wives, grasping hot iron balls.
They transform into jeweled vessels placed before the person.
Saying:
"I will follow you in death, entwined together, never to part."
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are born in the iron city, running east and west.
Iron serpents emerge with venom, coiling around their body, each segment blazing with fire.
They then think:
"May heaven pity me and send down sweet rain."
In response to this thought, it immediately rains large hot iron balls, entering through the neck and exiting through the feet.
Only after their sin is exhausted do they become poor, lonely, mute, and deaf people.
The number of years is as described for the Iron Cave.
Encountering a good spiritual friend, they arouse the bodhi mind.
The Sharp Stone Hell.
There are twenty-five stone mountains.
Each stone mountain has eight pools of water.
Each pool has five poisonous dragons.
Bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs,
śrāmaṇeras, śrāmaṇerikās,
śikṣamāṇās,
upāsakas, upāsikās,
and those of the ninety-five kinds of Brahmanical practices,
who violate minor precepts,
do not repent for a long time, and are without shame or remorse in their hearts.
When their life is about to end,
their heart feels full of qi, their abdomen distended like a drum.
Food and drink are regurgitated, water and broth cannot be swallowed.
They then think:
"Wouldn't it be joyful to get a sharp stone to block my throat?"
At that time, the hell guards transform into good physicians.
They break off sharp stones, making large medicinal pills, and place them in the person's mouth.
Telling them to close their mouth.
Their heart gives rise to joy.
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are born among the stone mountains.
Innumerable sharp stones enter from their back and exit through their chest.
The hell guards again use iron forks to pry open their mouth and insert stones inside.
Sixty billion births in one day and one night.
This is the birth retribution.
From here, when life ends, they fall into the Black Rope Hell.
The Black Rope Hell.
Eight hundred iron chains, eight hundred iron mountains.
Large iron pillars are erected, with chains tied at both ends.
Hell guards drive them, making them run on the iron ropes.
Unable to endure, they fall down into a cauldron of boiling water.
Driven to rise, parched and urgent, they drink molten iron and swallow stones while running.
In one day and one night, they undergo this suffering a total of one hundred thousand times.
After their sin is exhausted, they are born in the world as servants.
Encountering a good spiritual friend who expounds the true Dharma for them.
They attain arhatship.
The Drinking Molten Copper Hell.
One thousand two hundred kinds of multicolored copper chariots.
On each copper chariot are six thousand copper balls.
Due to stinginess, greed, jealousy, wrong views, and evil speech,
they do not give to parents, wife, children, relatives, or to anyone.
Their heart gives rise to stinginess and jealousy; seeing others gain benefit is like an arrow piercing their heart.
When such sinners are about to die,
they are often ill, emaciated, delirious, and talk in their sleep.
At that time, hell guards transform and bring fruit on a copper chariot to the sinner's place.
Obtaining it, they are joyful.
They then think:
"Obtaining this fine fruit is very much in accordance with my wish."
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are born on a copper chariot.
Not long after, they go and are born among copper mountains.
The copper chariot turns their neck.
Hell guards use pincers to pry open their mouth and make them drink molten copper.
Bewildered and fainting, they fall to the ground, crying out "Hungry! Hungry!"
Immediately, hell guards force their mouth open.
They place copper and iron balls in their mouth.
They swallow eighteen balls.
Each segment blazes with fire as they run east and west.
After seven days, only then does their life end.
Hell guards cry out:
"In your previous life,
you flattered, held wrong views, were stingy, greedy, and jealous.
Because of these causes and conditions, you receive the retribution of iron balls.
Or perhaps you once left home, violated minor precepts,
did not repent for a long time, and vainly consumed the faithful's offerings.
Because of these causes and conditions, you eat these iron balls.
For billions, thousands, and millions of years, this person's karmic retribution includes not recognizing water or grain.
After their punishment is completed, they are reborn among humans.
For five hundred lifetimes, their speech is stammering and unclear, unable to articulate properly.
Due to past habits, after eating they nibble on clods of earth.
After this, they encounter a good spiritual friend and arouse the bodhi mind.
First, trampling.
Previously trampled and killed people, now they are devoured by hell demons.
For two hundred years.
Second, mountain of knives.
Previously killed living beings, now they undergo punishment for two hundred years.
Third, careful discernment.
With angry mind, cursed people, considering them birds and beasts.
For five hundred years, an iron pestle strikes their mouth.
After their sin is exhausted, they are reborn with a human head and bird body.
Their mouth constantly speaks of sin.
Fourth, embracing knives and swords.
They themselves violated the precept against sexual misconduct.
And also violated against those who uphold precepts.
Fifth, boiling sand.
Previously covered living beings with hot ashes.
Sixth, boiling well.
The well water constantly boils.
With evil mind, used impure things to throw into the well.
After their sin is exhausted, for one hundred years they become frogs in the well.
Seventh, stove window hell guards.
Put people upside down into the stove window.
This woman, during her life,
used the hem of her garment to allure other men by looking at her shadow.
Eighth, mute demon.
Hell constantly burns iron to brand their tongue.
During life, when parents and teachers called, they did not respond.
After two hundred years, they are reborn as mute people.
Ninth, hot ashes.
Seven hundred li filled with hot ashes.
This person, during life, gave rise to lustful desire.
Sought to stay with a chaste woman but ultimately did not succeed.
Undergoes punishment for two hundred years.
Later reborn with sores and constant terror.
Tenth, boiling excrement.
Thirty thousand li filled with feces and urine.
Drives people into it.
Previously gave people good food,
but angrily said it was like eating filth.
Undergoes punishment for five hundred years as a pig.
Eleventh, putrid stench.
Two thousand five hundred li in length and breadth.
Filled with pus and blood.
This person, during life, with unwholesome mind entered a sage's room, breaking wind and emitting filth.
Undergoes punishment for two hundred and forty years.
Later reborn among poor and lowly people, their body constantly stinking.
Twelfth, impurity.
One thousand li in length and breadth, filled with mucus and saliva.
With arrogant mind, impure hands pinched incense to offer to great sages.
Later reborn among humans, constantly arrogant.
Thirteenth, impurity.
Six hundred li of pus.
During life, at mealtime,
there was rat feces, dog food, impurities,
thrown into clean food.
Undergoes punishment for two hundred years, after which reborn as a dog.
Fourteenth, black ear constant darkness.
During life, with unwholesome mind obstructed the Buddha's light.
Undergoes punishment for seven hundred years.
Fifteenth, forty thousand li in length and breadth.
Constantly hacked, shot, beaten, carved, pushed, and pounded.
This person, during life, committed the five heinous deeds.
Undergoes punishment spanning numerous kalpas.
If transferred among various hells,
thus also has a kalpa count of ten thousand years.
Sixteenth, mutual killing.
Wife kills husband, husband kills wife.
Mother kills child, child kills mother.
That person previously killed others' parents.
And also killed living beings' parents and children.
When reborn among humans,
their parents, children, and grandchildren all die early.
Seventeenth, hacking the body.
Constantly hacked by hell demons.
Because previously hacked living beings.
Later reborn, fond of encountering government officials.
Eighteenth, fire chariot.
This person previously burned and killed living beings.
Later reborn, they are burned.
Nineteenth, not knowing the Dharma.
Filled with ignorant people who hear the sound of the ghaṇṭā,
lie down with arrogant mind.
Later reborn in borderlands.
Twentieth, iron roasting.
Because roasted shrimp and crabs.
Later reborn short-lived.
The twenty-first is hungry ghosts.
Their bodies are forty li long.
Their bellies are like ten-thousand-hu baskets.
Their necks are ten li long.
They constantly suffer hunger and thirst, and their breath is always foul.
When they see food, it turns into charcoal.
Drink turns into pus and blood.
They still eat vegetarian food but do not uphold the vegetarian precepts.
Later, they are born for eight hundred lifetimes, often becoming ràkshasas.
The twenty-second is red-hot charcoal.
With a thieving mind, they take others' belongings, and their hands hold red-hot charcoal.
Later, they are born poor and lowly, being used by others.
The twenty-third is the cauldron of boiling water.
In life, with a malicious mind, they poured hot water on insects on the ground.
The twenty-fourth is the iron bed.
They committed adultery with others' wives and forced themselves upon women upholding precepts.
Men embrace copper pillars, women lie on iron beds.
The twenty-fifth is iron pellets.
They still roasted and boiled chicken and duck eggs.
Later, they are born constantly suffering from confusion and delusion.
The twenty-sixth is the haughty and arrogant hell.
In life, they were haughty and arrogant, consuming the faithful offerings of others.
Relying on their own virtue, they gave rise to a haughty and arrogant mind.
The twenty-seventh is black ears.
Hell demons dismember them joint by joint with knives.
They committed adultery with bhikṣus.
Later, they are born among lowly women.
For five hundred years, they become eunuchs.
The twenty-eighth is the freezing ice hell.
In life, they threw sentient beings into freezing cold places.
Later, they are born poor and lowly, often without clothes.
The twenty-ninth is the stone cave.
It is filled with smoke and fire.
With a malicious mind, they smoked and killed sentient beings.
The thirtieth is capture.
Ghosts and hell demons capture them because they killed lice and fleas with a hateful mind.
The thirty-first is crushing.
They crushed lice and fleas to death with a mountain.
Later, they are born with short lifespans.
The thirty-second is hot water poured on the body.
They wore fine clothes to seduce others' women.
After their sins are exhausted, they become birds and beasts.
The thirty-third is hungry ghosts.
Their bodies are thirty li long.
Below their throats is a goiter that bursts with pus, which they eat.
Sometimes they see good food.
Many ghosts compete to snatch it, so they cannot eat it.
When they obtained good food from others, they did not first offer it to the senior monks to eat.
Later, they are born poor.
The thirty-fourth is hungry ghosts.
Their bodies are ten li or five li long.
Their body hair is sharp and hard.
They were stingy and did not give food, saying they had none when they did.
Later, they are born poor and lowly, often without food and drink.
The thirty-fifth is evil dogs.
There are many evil dogs with teeth as sharp as swords.
Hell demons call the dogs to compete in biting them.
In life, they called dogs to bite and kill sentient beings.
Later, when born as humans, they are often bitten by dogs.
The thirty-sixth is iron stakes.
They drive people to tread on them.
In life, they harbored poison and looked at their parents and teachers with malice.
Later, they are born among poisonous snakes.
The thirty-seventh is skinning.
Ghosts constantly skin them with sharp knives.
In life, with a malicious mind, they stripped people of their clothes and bedding.
And skinned sentient beings.
Later, when born among humans, they are often stripped and robbed by others.
The thirty-eighth is hanging upside down.
Hell guards take people and hang them upside down.
In life, they hung sentient beings upside down.
The thirty-ninth is animals.
Hell demons pour molten copper into their mouths.
They incurred debts and refused to repay them.
Later, for five hundred years,
they become oxen, horses, slaves, and servants for humans.
They often receive whippings and beatings.
The fortieth is plowing the body.
Hell demons plow their bodies with iron plows.
In life, they plowed the land and injured sentient beings.
With a malicious mind, they cursed and reviled.
The forty-first is eye piercing.
Hell demons constantly pierce their eyes with iron arrows.
In life, with a malicious mind, they looked at their parents with evil eyes.
Later, when born among humans, their eyes are often crossed.
The forty-second is weapons.
Hell demons hack and shoot.
This person in life killed others with a hateful mind.
Later, when born among humans, they often suffer hacking and shooting.
The forty-third is cutting and stabbing.
Hell demons cut their flesh while alive.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, cut others' flesh.
After their sins are exhausted, when born as humans, they often suffer cutting and stabbing.
The forty-fourth is iron grinding.
Hell demons grind people with iron grindstones.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, ground and killed insects in the grindstone.
The forty-fifth is tumbling.
It is filled with iron grindstones.
Hell demons drive people into the grindstones to grind them.
The forty-sixth is tumbling.
This person in life,
saw sentient beings falling into the tumbling pit,
and with a malicious mind vowed not to save them.
Later, when born among humans, their bodies are yellow and withered.
The forty-seventh is stone mortar.
Guards drive them into the mortar and pound them.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, pounded and killed sentient beings.
After their sins are exhausted, they become snails and clams.
The forty-eighth is arrogance.
They have human heads and snake bodies.
This person in life lay on the ground while reciting scriptures.
The forty-ninth is the water hell.
The water is stagnant and does not flow.
This person in life held people underwater until they drowned and died.
The fiftieth is dwarfs.
Hell demons press people's heads with stones.
This person in life had an arrogant mind.
They made their parents and teachers rely on them,
and made their children speak disrespectfully.
The fifty-first is iron clubs.
Hell demons constantly make their bodies club iron; this person in life, with a malicious mind, killed lice and fleas.
The fifty-second is terror.
They are constantly terrified by ox-headed and horse-faced guards.
This person in life often terrified others.
The fifty-third is iron stakes.
Iron stakes are placed at the bottom of the water.
Hell demons drive people into the water to pierce their bodies, causing bleeding.
In life, out of jealousy, they placed stakes to injure people.
The fifty-fourth is drinking molten copper.
In life, with an arrogant mind, they mimicked their parents' and teachers' speech.
Later, they often stutter.
The fifty-fifth is iron arrows.
Hell demons pierce their eyes with iron arrows.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, pierced the pupils of sentient beings.
After their sins are exhausted, they become blind people.
The fifty-sixth is the iron fork hell.
Hell demons fork people with iron forks.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, forked fish and other sentient beings.
The fifty-seventh is maggots.
They nibble on human bodies.
This person in life, out of jealousy like maggots, injured people.
And the wealth and property of the six domestic animals.
After their sins are exhausted, when born as humans, they suffer from malignant sores.
The fifty-eighth is severing hands.
Hell demons sever their two hands with sharp knives.
This person in life, with an arrogant mind,
used unclean hands to handle scriptures.
The fifty-ninth is weeping.
Hell guards come to terrify them, making them weep.
This person in life constantly worried about money to pursue lustful desires.
Later, when born as humans, they constantly suffer from lack of wealth.
The sixtieth is iron shackles.
Hell demons constantly shackle their bodies with iron shackles.
This person in life shackled and killed sentient beings.
The sixty-first is molten copper.
Hell demons pour molten copper into their mouths.
This person in life, with a malicious mind,
lied, engaged in divisive speech, cursed harshly, and spoke frivolously.
After their sins are exhausted, when born as humans, their breath is always foul.
The sixty-second is molten copper poured on hands.
This person in life did not respect the Dao in their heart.
They used unclean hands to handle the robes of śramaṇas.
The sixty-third is shooting the body.
Hell demons shoot them with arrows.
This person in life, with a malicious mind, shot and killed sentient beings.
The sixty-fourth is non-selective; there are five kings in total.
The first is Suí Wáng.
The second is Jié Wáng.
The third is Chǒu Wáng.
The fourth is Zìrán Wáng.
The fifth is Zhòngshēng Wáng.
They all developed faith in the Mahāyāna and vowed to save sentient beings in hell.
Those whose sins in the various hells are exhausted come here.
Their past actions and the extent of their sins are judged.
They shed their hell bodies and receive an intermediate existence form, like a three-year-old child.
Then, according to their karma, they receive rebirth from parents.
The Living Great Hell.
With malicious hearts and angry disputes, they stab each other with spears.
Iron claws tear at each other, blood smears and spreads.
Pain and poison press urgently, stifling with no awareness.
A cold wind blows in.
The jailers call the living sinners back to life.
Thus it is named the Living Hell.
The beings here in previous lives delighted in killing living creatures, cattle, sheep, birds, and beasts.
For the sake of fields, houses, kingdoms, territories, money, wealth, and other benefits, they killed and harmed each other.
They receive this retribution of punishment.
The Meeting Great Hell.
Rākṣasa jailers.
Assume various forms with heads of evil beasts.
And come to devour, bite, and gnaw the sinners.
Two mountains come together, hot iron wheels crush.
Hot iron mortars pound, also like pressing oil.
Gathered flesh becomes piles, flowing blood becomes pools.
Eagles, vultures, tigers, and wolves each come to pull and tear.
These people in previous lives killed many living beings and now receive this form of hell.
Also, using power and influence to bully, oppress, and crush the weak.
Receive the punishment of two mountains coming together.
Stingy, greedy, angry, hateful, foolish, ignorant, fearful, and terrified.
Judging matters lightly or heavily, not according to proper principle.
Or destroying the right path.
Receive the punishment of hot iron wheels crushing and hot iron mortars pounding.
The fourth and fifth are named Crying and Great Crying.
In this great hell, the sinners within.
Rākṣasa jailers, yellow necks, red eyes, fire issuing from within.
Wearing vermilion clothes, bodies and flesh hard and strong.
Run and shoot at sinners.
Sinners mad with terror, kowtowing, begging for mercy.
Calling "Great General," hoping for a little pity and compassion.
They are taken into the hot iron ground hell.
Extending a hundred yojanas in length and breadth.
Driven and beaten, driven to run, feet all scorched.
Fat and marrow flow out like pressed butter oil.
Iron clubs strike the forehead, brains flow out like a broken cheese jar.
Again taken into iron tower rooms.
Black smoke comes to suffocate.
Piling and pressing upon each other, wishing to get out.
The door already closed, great cries and wails, voices never ceasing.
These people in previous lives deceived with scales and measures.
Unlawfully judged matters, received things in trust and did not return them.
Oppressed and bullied the lowly, tormented the poor, making them wail and cry.
Destroyed others' cities and towns, ruined people's settlements.
Harmed, robbed, and plundered, causing the whole city to cry out.
Deceitfully lured them out and then harmed them again.
Now they receive the Crying Hell.
Smoked and killed cave-dwelling creatures, imprisoned in dark dungeons.
Or in dark smoky caves, smoked and killed them.
Or threw them into wells, robbed and plundered others' wealth.
All receive the retribution of punishment in the Great Crying Hell.
The sixth and seventh, Hot and Great Hot Hells.
Within are two great copper cauldrons.
Full of boiling salty water.
Rākṣasa jailers throw sinners into them.
Feet up, head down, joints and bones disintegrate.
Taken out with forks, cold wind blows to revive, then thrown into charcoal pits.
Or placed in boiling ash.
Taken out from the ash, placed in hot sand.
Also with pus and blood, they boil themselves.
Taken out from the charcoal pits, thrown onto flaming beds, forcibly driven to sit.
Eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and all pores issue fire.
These people in past lives harassed and troubled parents, teachers, elders, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and all good people.
Troubled them, making their hearts hot, now receive the retribution of the Hot Hell.
Or some in previous lives boiled and killed living silkworm cocoons.
Or boiled pigs and sheep alive.
Or impaled people's abdomens with wood and roasted them alive.
Or burned mountains, wildernesses, and various settlements, Buddhist temples, monasteries, and deva shrines.
Or pushed living beings into fire pits.
Therefore they are born in this hell.
The Avīci Hell extends four thousand miles in length and breadth.
Its place is the deepest.
Jailers, rākṣasas, peel the skin from the head down to the feet.
With five hundred nails, nail the body like stretching cowhide.
Hot iron fire carts crush their bodies.
Driven into fire pits, made to embrace charcoal and come out.
Sharp knives, swords, and spears fly into their bodies, confused, stifled, withered, and cooked.
Or topple, crawl, and fall down.
These people in past conduct created many great evils.
The five grave offenses, heavy sins, cutting off good roots.
Calling the Dharma non-Dharma, calling non-Dharma Dharma.
Destroying causes, destroying effects, hating and envying good people.
Enter this hell, receive punishment most severe.
